finding: E3 says tests reset the dataset; the build profile forbids a reset and asks for unique run ids. The two writers follow different sources.

D11 with D3: for a DEPRECATED vocabulary the deprecated-reference warning can recommend the very version it warns about ('version 1 is deprecated. Use version 1').
D12 gives the S7 text only with a version number. The text for a reference without a version is not fixed.
The OpenAPI and D44 fix urn:problem-type:belgif types for 400, 404, 500 and 503; project rule API-46 asks for urn:problem-type:simpl types. Which wins is not decided.
No decision says what GET, PATCH or DELETE return for a name in the path that breaks the D37 pattern: 400 or 404.
D23 does not say what a click on the column that is already the active sort does: start at ascending or reverse the order.
On POST /vocabularies the order of the 409 duplicate-name check and the 400 content checks is not fixed.
On POST .../versions and the PATCH operations the order of 404 and the field checks (400, 413, 415) is not fixed (D46 lists them together).
Only the 'version' form field is decided (D7). Other unknown form fields and JSON properties are not decided.
D21 covers unknown query parameters on GET only. Query parameters on POST, PATCH and DELETE, and a parameter given twice, are not decided.
Rule S4 does not say whether two skos:prefLabel literals without a language tag on one subject count as the same language.
Names are unique ignoring case (D37), but no decision says whether a path lookup ignores case.
Problem texts not fixed by any decision: version not found, external namespace conflict, field messages, 405 and unknown path.

External vocabularies: case-insensitive name uniqueness, an alias equal to the own namespace, duplicate aliases, how aliasUris is encoded in multipart, description length, and clashes with internal names are not decided.
The base IRI for relative IRIs in uploaded Turtle is not decided.
The precision of stored and returned times is not decided.
The collation of the name sort is not decided (code point puts 'AZ' before 'Ab').
The prev link on a page beyond the last page is not decided.

UI texts and steps not fixed: menu label, confirmation on a status change, date display format, not-found and 5xx messages, button and field labels, the status-change action label, the link back to the list.
D13 asks for syntax errors 'with line and column', but common browser Turtle parsers report no column.
SIMPL-28680 is out of scope by D1, but its six criteria are still in the component's live set.
The decisions do not say whether Submit is disabled while a field error shows (D13 against D37).

finding: The status of /actuator paths on the API port is not decided.
Paths with an encoded slash or a control character are rejected before routing (400, no issues); not decided.
A non-standard method without a token gives 405 while PUT gives 401; D17 does not cover the order.
No decision gives availability, recovery time or recovery point (NFR-06); the code writer chose them.
The decided limits are not in the OpenAPI file, so fuzzing and clients do not see them (D39).
D27 stores the email as createdBy, and the build writes it to INFO logs.
D43 is met with an in-process lock, which is safe for one backend instance only (ARCH-07).
The restore script can leave an empty store when the load fails.
The reference check sends one store query per referenced vocabulary, with no bound per upload.
The test realm has one client, which carries the audience mapper, so the 401 for a wrong audience or issuer (E5) cannot be tested.
The in-process lock of D43 forces one replica (D81); ARCH-07 is not met.
The store accepts SPARQL Update without credentials and the decisions are silent on store access (E3).
A request that matches no entry of the role table passes the role check (fails open).
List and search queries fetch every row and page in memory (NFR-05, Q4).
No metrics, and the correlation id is not forwarded to the store or the identity provider (NFR-08, MSV-09, MSV-10).
No decision says whether the build delivers an LDM, a PDM for an RDF store, or an OpenAPI that shows the decided changes (D79).
